summary: M4-S02 tested after its W4 ambiguity block was closed at the source (commit a18f9164d, admin/entitlements-and-milestones v1.1.2). Both always-on structural checks passed: xml 4/4 files parse; manifest two-way consistent (3 derived members, all literal, all covered in both directions, 0 wildcards, no coverage-gap exclusions applicable). The one declared checker (check_entitlements_and_milestones.py --manifest-dir artefacts --strict, scope build) ran verbatim from the build directory and exited 0 with 0 errors, 0 warnings, 2 info notes (W4, now INFO not WARN, so --strict does not promote it); check-outputs reported ok:true, 5/5 declared outputs present, non-empty, and the 4 XML/meta-XML among them parse. The one manual test was checked against the Given/When/Then shape and found usable (names an observable, boolean outcome) and deferred verbatim to the M4 milestone gate, not ticked. Step set to tested. This run added no new finding beyond what artefacts/M4-S02/deploy-order.md sections 1-7 already carry to the gate as open items.
confidence_rationale: Step 7 rubric, HIGH row: the one declared acceptance test ran and the one manual test was correctly classified, both always-on checks completed, and every result came from an exit code this agent observed directly. No MEDIUM trigger fired: no command test was refused (none was declared), no manifest exclusion was needed for a coverage-gap type (none of the two types present -- EntitlementProcess, MilestoneType -- lacks a standalone file or manifest member), and check-outputs reported no missing, empty or malformed declared output. No LOW trigger fired: the one declared checker resolved to exactly one existing script, the artefact directory holds 6 files (4 metadata/manifest + 2 markdown), and every exit code was captured to tests/M4-S02/.

process_observations.observation: The checker's W4 finding is not being waved through by a weakened rule -- it is consistent with this step's own recorded design. milestone-completion-decision.md records D10: the First Response milestone is completed by an after-update Apex trigger built in M4-S05, not by a workflow alert or field update, and no clarification anywhere in this build names a milestone notification's recipient, offset, sender or template. An action-less <timeTriggers>/<successActions> pair on both processes is therefore the designed shape, not a gap the rule change papered over. Re-running the same command this session reproduced the identical 0 error/0 warning/2 info result recorded in deploy-order.md section 0.

The manifest is fully explicit -- no wildcard members -- despite both EntitlementProcess and MilestoneType supporting the * wildcard per the skill's own metadata reference. deploy-order.md section 1 records this was a deliberate choice so the step's own manifest acceptance test can assert two-way member<->file consistency, which a wildcard member cannot be checked against in the manifest-to-file direction. All 3 derived members (2 EntitlementProcess, 1 MilestoneType) matched literal <members> entries with nothing left over in either direction.

Standard's minutesToComplete (720) is a derived value, not an answered one -- Q38 says '1 business day' and nothing in this build converts a business day to minutes directly; deploy-order.md section 3 documents the derivation chain (US Support calendar, 08:00-20:00, 12 open hours x 60). The checker's E1 rule only confirms the field is present and numeric; it cannot and does not confirm 720 is the number the Process Owner meant. This is unchanged by this test run and remains open at the M4 gate exactly as deploy-order.md records it.

This step's declared checker is scope build (--manifest-dir artefacts, not artefacts/M4-S02), and the intent and the command agree -- the W3 BusinessHours cross-reference this checker also makes needs M4-S01's settings file, which lives outside this step's own artefacts. Recorded here because the same class of cross-referential-checker-at-wrong-scope defect is what standards/build-orchestration.md section 5 warns against for four named checkers; this one is not on that list but behaves the same way, and step scope alone (as v3's superseded test ran it) silently produced 4 W6 warnings instead of a real cross-reference, per deploy-order.md section 0's kept record.

Entitlement Management's org-level switch (settings/Entitlement.settings-meta.xml: enableEntitlements, enableEntitlementVersioning, enableMilestoneStoppedTime) is owned by no step in this plan, per deploy-order.md section 5. Every file this step writes is inert without enableEntitlements on. This agent cannot resolve who owns it -- that is a plan-scoping decision for the M4 gate, not a test-time judgment.

The file names and package.xml member forms this step wrote (First_Response_Premier, mixed case, no _v suffix) are UNVERIFIED against what a real org retrieve would return -- deploy-order.md sections 4.1-4.2 record that the skill documents the file name as NameNorm (lowercased) plus a version suffix when versioning is on, and this build is design-only with no org to retrieve against. Not resolvable by this test run; the checker has no rule for file-name casing and none was expected to fire.
M4-S02 is tested; the doc keeper is the next stage of the loop.
